{
  "research_question": "How do different stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) affect mouse navigation performance metrics including Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": [
    "Combined",
    "ICMS Only",
    "Dim Visual Only",
    "Bright Visual Only",
    "Sham"
  ],
  "response_variables": [
    "Time-to-Target",
    "Success",
    "Path Efficiency",
    "Average Speed",
    "AD"
  ],
  "descriptive_findings": [
    "The Sham group exhibited the lowest Success rate (0.273) and the highest Time-to-Target (4.68s), indicating significantly impaired navigation compared to all other groups.",
    "Success rates were highest in the Bright Visual Only group (0.785), followed closely by the Combined group (0.780), while Dim Visual Only and ICMS Only groups showed lower success (0.673 and 0.685 respectively).",
    "Time-to-Target was fastest in the Combined group (2.56s) and Bright Visual Only group (2.61s), whereas the Sham group was the slowest (4.68s).",
    "Path Efficiency was highest in the Bright Visual Only group (0.504) and Combined group (0.502), with the Sham group showing the lowest efficiency (0.308).",
    "Average Speed was highest in the Combined group (12.83) and Bright Visual Only group (12.68), while the Sham group moved slowest (10.74).",
    "Angular Dispersion (AD) was highest in the Combined group (0.399) and Bright Visual Only group (0.387), while the Sham group showed the lowest dispersion (0.236), suggesting tighter turning angles or different path dynamics in the control group.",
    "Sample sizes varied significantly, with the Combined group (n=48,846) dominating the dataset, while the Sham group had the smallest sample (n=3,505)."
  ],
  "strongest_group_differences": [
    "The Sham group shows a drastic reduction in Success (0.273) compared to the average of the other four groups (~0.729), a difference of approximately 0.456.",
    "Time-to-Target in the Sham group (4.68s) is nearly double that of the Combined group (2.56s) and Bright Visual Only group (2.61s).",
    "Path Efficiency in the Sham group (0.308) is substantially lower than in the visual stimulation groups (0.502-0.504), indicating much less direct paths to the target.",
    "Bright Visual Only and Combined paradigms yield statistically and practically similar performance profiles across all metrics, suggesting visual input alone is the primary driver of performance in this context."
  ],
  "practical_interpretation": "Visual stimulation (Bright Visual Only) and the Combined paradigm (likely combining visual and ICMS) are highly effective at restoring or maintaining mouse navigation capabilities, resulting in high success rates and efficient paths. ICMS Only and Dim Visual Only provide partial benefits but are inferior to full visual input. The Sham condition demonstrates severe navigation deficits, characterized by low success, slow movement, inefficient paths, and distinct angular dispersion patterns, confirming the necessity of the stimulation for normal navigation performance.",
  "limitations": [
    "The dataset is heavily imbalanced, with the Combined group comprising over 60% of the data (48,846 out of 76,655), which may skew overall summary statistics and reduce statistical power for detecting subtle effects in smaller groups like Sham.",
    "The analysis relies solely on descriptive statistics (means and SDs) provided in the artifacts; inferential statistics (e.g., ANOVA, post-hoc tests) are not available to confirm the significance of observed differences.",
    "The interpretation of AD (Angular Dispersion) is based on mean values only; the distribution shape and variance within groups are unknown, which is critical for understanding navigation stability.",
    "No time-series or trajectory data is available to analyze the specific sequence of movements, only aggregated path efficiency."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Conduct a one-way ANOVA for each of the five response variables followed by post-hoc pairwise comparisons (e.g., Tukey's HSD) to formally test for significant differences between the five stimulation paradigms, specifically focusing on the Sham group versus the stimulation groups. Additionally, perform a power analysis or bootstrap resampling to account for the severe sample size imbalance between the Combined group and the other groups."
}
